AMENDED AGENDA

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  MAY 19, 2026 – 7:00 P.M.
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5938 KAUFFMAN AVENUE - TEMPLE CITY

Pursuant to AB 2449, this meeting will be available via teleconference. Members of the public
may attend and participate in the meeting either in person or through the teleconference
option.

To listen to the meeting telephonically, please call 1-669-900-6833, Meeting 870-5534-8485 or
through City’s live webcast on YouTube: ConnectWithTC www.youtube.com/@ConnectWithTC

PROCEDURE TO ADDRESS CITY COUNCIL:
In person: Members of the Public who wish to address the City Council may do so by completing
a Speaker Request Form, indicating the agenda item number and submitting it to the City Clerk.
Unless waived by Council, t here is a 3-minute time limit on each speaker with a maximum
period of 30 minutes for comments on any subject.

Written Comment: Written public comments received by 5pm on the day of the meeting will be
provided to the City Council and made part of the meeting record. Written public comments will
not be read aloud by city staff or City Council.

Teleconference: Telephonically by calling 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 870-5534-8485. Your
microphone will be unmuted during one of the comment periods outlined below. Please request
to be added to the speaker list and you will be called upon to make a comment. The time for
public comment on any item will extend one minute after the end of the last comment to provide a
reasonable period of time for members of the public to join the call. Should there be no
commenters on an item, the one-minute period will commence when the time for public comment
is announced.
You have the opportunity to address the City Council at the following times:
  •  Agenda item: at the time the Council considers the agenda item;
  •  Non-agenda item: at the time for PUBLIC COMMENTS. Please note that while the
  City Council values your comments, pursuant to the Brown Act, the Council cannot
  take action on any item not listed on the agenda; and
  • Public Hearing: at the time for public hearings under PUBLIC HEARING.
The listing of any item on the agenda includes the authority of the Council to take action
on such item and to approve, disapprove, or give directions on any item.
   City Council Agenda
  May 19, 2026
  Page 2 of 8

NOTICE: Staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business of this
Agenda are available for viewing on the City’s website at templecityca.gov and are on file and
available for review during regular office hours in the Office of the City Clerk located at City Hall,
9701 Las Tunas Drive, Temple City, California. Written documentation submitted to the City
Council after distribution of the agenda packet can be obtained at the City Clerk’s Office during
regular office hours.

ACCESSIBILITY: In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special
assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk at (626) 285-2171.
Notification 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements
to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

TO WATCH REGULAR MEETINGS LIVE OR RECORDED, VISIT:
https://www.youtube.com/@ConnectWithTC

AGENDA NOTIFICATION SUBSCRIPTION:
If you wish to receive an agenda email notification, please email your request to
cityclerk@templecityca.gov or call (626) 285-2171.

  B. PLANNING COMMISSION ACTIONS - MEETING OF APRIL 28, 2026

  The City Council is requested to receive and file the Planning Commission Actions

  C. CONSIDERATION OF ANNUAL RATE ADJUSTMENT REQUEST BY ATHENS
  SERVICES FOR SOLID WASTE COLLECTION

  The City Council is requested to approve a rate adjustment for solid waste
  collection services to become effective July 1, 2026.

  Recommendation:  Approve a 4.40% rate adjustment for solid waste
  collection services to become effective July 1,
  2026.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  D. FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH WEST COAST ARBORIST, INC.
  FOR TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES
  The City Council is requested to approve a first amendment to the agreement with
  West Coast Arborist, Inc. (WCA) for tree maintenance services.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to the agreement with West Coast Arborist to
  extend the contract an additional three years and increase rates 2.9% with a
  term end date of June 30, 2029; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the First Amendment to the agreement
  with West Coast Arborist, Inc. (WCA) for tree maintenance services.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  E. CO-SPONSOR THE 2026 HI AUTUMN FESTIVAL WITH WORLD JOURNAL LA,
  LLC
  The City Council is requested to consider and approve co-sponsorship of the 2026
  Hi Autumn Festival with World Journal LA, LLC.
  Recommendation:

  1. Approve hosting and co-sponsorship of a 2026 Hi Autumn Festival (Festival)
  with World Journal LA, LLC (World Journal) on Saturday, September 19 through
  Sunday, September 20, 2026;

  2. Approve the temporary parking restriction on the north side of Las Tunas Drive
  between Kauffman Avenue and Golden West Avenue adjacent to Temple City
  Park and a parking restriction on the west side of Golden West Avenue adjacent
  to Temple City Park on September 18 at 9:00 a.m. through September 20, 2026
  at 11:59 p.m.;

  3. Waive all fees and deposits for the use of Temple City Park and the Performing
  Arts Pavilion;

  4. Waive all fees and authorize city staff to hang a street banner on Las Tunas
  Drive from August 10 to September 20, 2026;

  5. Approve use of the city’s outdoor movie screen and equipment;

  6. Approve the use of the City Seal and city logo for advertising and promotional
  materials; and

  7. Grant World Journal LA, LLC a special event permit with the conditions and
  responsibilities stated in the staff report and authorize the City Manager to place
  additional conditions if necessary.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  F. APPROVAL OF A LETTER OF SUPPORT FOR THE JOINT POWERS
  INSURANCE AUTHORITY COALITION TO PROTECT COMMUNITY SERVICES
  The City Council is requested to consider and approve a letter of support for the
  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority, Coalition to Protect Community
  Services, advocating for liability reform in the state legislature.

  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority.
  Attachment:  Staff Report

  G. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-5873 DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER
  AND ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR AS AUTHORIZED AGENTS ON
  BEHALF OF THE CITY FOR THE PURPOSE OF SEEKING REIMBURSEMENT
  FUNDS FROM FEDERAL AND STATE DISASTER AND EMERGENCY FUNDS
  The City Council is requested to consider and adopt a resolution designating City's
  authorized agents to engage with Federal Emergency management Agency and
  California Governor's Office of Emergency Services.

  Recommendation:  Adopt Resolution No. 26-26-5873 to designate
  the City Manager and the Administrative Services
  Director as authorized agents on behalf of the
  City to engage with Federal Emergency
  Management Agency and California Governor’s
  Office of Emergency Services for the purpose of
  obtaining federal and state disaster and
  emergency funds.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  H. APPROVAL OF CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENTS WITH FAMILY
  PROMISE OF SAN GABRIEL VALLEY TO ADMINISTER THE CITY’S
  PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION PROGRAMS TO ASSIST
  FAMILIES EXPERIENCING OR AT RISK OF HOMELESSNESS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2026-27
  The City Council is requested to consider and approve agreements for
  administration of the City's Permanent Local Housing Allocation Programs to assist
  families experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a Consultant Services Agreement with Family Promise of San Gabriel
  Valley (“Family Promise”) for case management of a program assisting Temple
  City families for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the previously mentioned Consultant
  Services Agreement in an amount not to exceed $36,116;

  3. Approve a Consultant Services Agreement with Family Promise to assist
  Temple City families with rental and move-in assistance for FY 2026-27; and

  I. VISA CARD REPORT

  Recommendation: receive and file

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  J. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 26-5874 APPROVING PAYMENT OF BILLS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2025-26
  The City Council is requested to adopt Resolution No. 26-5874 authorizing the
  payment of bills for fiscal year 2025-26.

  Recommendation:  Adopt Resolution No. 26-5874 authorizing the
  payment of bills for fiscal year 2025-26.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

8. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. PUBLIC HEARING – ASSEMBLY BILL 2561: FY 2025/26 LOCAL PUBLIC

  Presenter:  City Manager
